recipes.name: Winter Leek and Potato Soup
ingredients_raw: 2 tablespoons butter, or more if needed
salt and ground black pepper to taste

steps.text: Melt butter in a pot over medium heat. Add leeks and onion; cook and stir until tender, about 5 minutes.
Add potatoes and chicken broth; simmer until potatoes are tender, 20 to 25 minutes.
Stir in half-and-half; simmer until slightly thickened, about 15 minutes more.
Stir in Cheddar cheese, parsley, garlic powder, salt, and black pepper until cheese is melted, about 5 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Winter Leek and Potato Soup
raw_recipe.description: This winter leek and potato soup recipe is a one-pot wonder. It’s creamy and cheesy. Store-bought chicken broth makes this potato leek soup a breeze.

review.reviewBody:
Excellent soup after my alterations! Everyone loved it! My initial reading of this recipe alerted me that it would be a very bland tasting soup. My only alterations were that I used 2 pounds of Yukon Gold potatoes, added 1 sliced celery stalk and added a large bay leaf. I also substituted the garlic powder with 4 garlic cloves that I minced and sautéed with the leeks and onions. I used 6 ounces of shredded sharp cheddar cheese and omitted the parsley. I offered crumbled cooked bacon, fresh snipped chives and prepared garlic-Parmesan croutons as options for diners to top their soup serving with. Next time, I will use individual sized shepherd loaves as serving bowls and make homemade garlic-Parmesan croutons out of the scooped bread from the shepherd loaves.

Tips:
Yukon Gold potatoes won't get mushy like russet potatoes will when boiling them. Use russet potatoes if you want a thick soup and mash them when they are tender.

Rinse the leeks in a bowl of cold water so to remove any sand, remove the leeks and wring dry in towels.

Keep the cubed potatoes in a bowl of cold water till needed.

Always turn off the heat before stirring in the cheese so that the cheese won't separate.

I made this recipe pretty much as is without adding the cheddar cheese and since I did not have half and half I had to make it myself with 1/3 whole milk and 1/3 heavy whipping cream. Whit that said, this soup is restaurant quality! Hands down. I will make it again. My only suggestion is to add chives instead of parsley. Once I blended it with a hand blender, I noticed it begged for chives! It is creamy and velvety! I had a small piece of celery which I chopped and added. I personally think the cheddar is unnecessary it could cover the flavor of the leeks.

This is fantastic! I also used fresh minced garlic, a bit of cayenne pepper, no bay leaf, and used immersion blender a little leaving some potato chunks. Stirred cheddar cheese into individual bowls and crumbled bacon atop homemade croutons! YUM! It's a keeper!!
4 cloves fresh garlic, more herbs, celery, white cheddar herb cheese, then i pureed in blender

I took the advice of some of the reviews to add some extra ingredients. I added two chopped garlic cloves cooked with the leeks and onions. I simmered with a bay leaf. I garnished with crumbled bacon and a sprinkle of cayenne pepper.
Everything else was done the same as the recipe. It was absolutely delicious!

It was so delicious! I added garlic chunks rather than powder and used 3 leeks. Mashed the potatoes up a bit as well. I only used the cheese as a garnish on top with a bit of bacon. It was a bit hit!!!

A good, simple to make potato soup. I used some turkey stock made from our Thanksgiving turkey, which was a much richer and flavorful stock than packaged chicken broth. I noticed that there are a lot of mentions of the soup being too bland, and I think my stock was the reason it was not. My other change was that I ran the immersion blender in the soup for a bit to puree part of the potatoes and leeks, as I like it thicker, but still left plenty of chunks. Very good and I'll make this again with leftover holiday turkey stock!

Loved it. Added a stalk of chopped celery, pinch of cayenne pepper, pinch of thyme and when emulsified with hand blender when potatoes ready. I put the remainder of herbal cream cheese spread into it then grated a hunk of Monterey Jack cheese and lastly 10% coffee cream about half a cup. A bit of fresh chopped parsley....fabulous. The pinch of cayenne pepper lends just a pinch of heat but not spicey. Will make this recipe again and just add whatever is left over in the fridge.

I plan on making this again. It was delectable. I use an immersion blender and I can control how smooth or chunky I want the soup. 

I saved the dark green leafy parts of the leeks and carefully cleaned them. I added them to some other vegetable peels I had, and made the most delicious vegetable broth.

We liked this soup a lot. After reading some of the other reviews, I made a couple of minor changes. I pureed the soup with an immersion blender once the potatoes were cooked. Then, I didn't add cream and cheddar cheese but replaced both with Boursin cheese. It was really yummy!

This was a great hit with both my husband and I...i added celeri leaves extra parsley for color and flavor and also added minced garlic..i did pass the hand blender a few times to give it the thickness..didn't find the table cream to thicken!...otherwise its a keeper for us!
Good base soup, improved with modifications to taste.
I also added broccoli that needed to be used up. Delicious

I make this all the time but swap out veggies with the seasons. Diced carrots frozen peas, even broccoli florets are great in this soup. I've also added shredded chicken or ham. I've added cubed cod fish as well in the last 10 minutes of cooking. A hint Dill weed or summer savory are amazing additions to this soup.
Very tasty! I used yellow potatoes because of their starch and found they needed to be cooked for about 30 minutes more.

Taste was awesome and very easy to make. I didn’t use the parsley and opted out of the cheese. After we had a bowl my wife blended up the rest, of course made it real thick and creamy. Next time will blend half and mix it in the rest.

I make the soup exactly exactly as written and love it. I always make a recipe the way it’s written first, and then if I want more of something or less of something else, I’ll add or subtract it the next time. I have a pet peeve about people changing the original recipe and then giving it a rating. Admittedly part of that pet peeve comes from the fact that I have a recipe on allrecipes. Virtually everyone who made the recipe as written, gives it five stars. The only three and four star reviews I get are from people who totally changed the recipe. So they’re giving their recipe the three or four star review. My request is that if you change a recipe, don’t rate it. Just rate it if you made it as written. Thanks.
Yummy to my tummy. I roasted the potatoes it was delicious😋
